bull_bear.body: Prioritizing capex for high-margin segments (wind, industrial, PV); maintaining strong liquidity (>Rs.350cr); no dividend or buyback mentioned; disciplined, value-driven allocation
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: US tariff uncertainty (25-26% on auto components), global CV/farm equipment demand slowdown, delayed infrastructure spending impacting off-highway, execution risk in new capacity ramp-up
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, proactive, and strategically focused; emphasizes diversification, value-addition, and new business wins; dismisses tariff impact as manageable; bullish on medium-term 15-18% growth from new products
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Despite 59% forging utilization, EBITDA margin held via high machining share (88%) and premium product mix; deemed exports flat, but new direct farm exports to Europe are fresh wins, not conversions; PV business is scaling rapidly with new product lines (front steering knuckles, suspension) beyond crankshafts
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Capex has largely been funded by operating cash accruals: cumulative FY21-FY26 OCF/EBITDA of 64%, rising to 94% in FY26; deck states 'healthy operating cash accruals have largely funded capex'.
- Balance sheet described as a 'fortress': FY26 Debt/Equity 0.15x, Net Debt/EBITDA -0.19x, net worth Rs. 2,128 Crs, AA Stable rating, and current liquidity surplus of ~Rs. 400 Cr+ which the deck says exceeds the primary capital raised during the IPO.
- FY26 return ratios: ROCE 18.2% and ROE 15.2%, framed as maintained through disciplined capital allocation with 'further upside from utilisation ramp-up'; gross fixed asset turnover has drifted from 1.2 (FY21) to 1.0 (FY26) during the capex build.
- Stated philosophy of 'judicious capital allocation and maintaining a strong balance sheet to create value', with balance-sheet flexibility explicitly held for both organic and inorganic growth, including growth 'inorganically through strategic acquisitions and alliances'.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: CV: 39% rev, -mid single-digit YoY (global weakness); Farm: 32% rev, +high single-digit YoY (India strength, exports negligible); Off-Highway: 10% rev, -mid single-digit (India), -10-12% (EU/US); Industrials: 13% rev, +strong growth (wind, power, O&G); PV: 6% rev, ramping fast, targeting 8-10% of total rev in 2 yrs
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Describes itself as the '2nd Largest' producer of crankshafts in India for commercial vehicle and high horsepower industrial applications, and the '3rd Largest' engineering-led manufacturer of complex and safety-critical heavy forged and high-precision machined components in India.
- Stated strategic transition is 'from a forging led player to a leading manufacturer of machined components in India', with in-house design and fungible production lines cited as the enabler of continuous value addition.
- Moat framed as 'HIGH ENTRY BARRIERS': capital-intensive business, lengthy customer and product approval processes, selective supplier qualification by global leaders given high switching cost/risk, and precision requirements (machined-product tolerance range 0.005 mm to 0.2 mm).
- Second company in India to have a 14,000 tonne press; ability to forge parts up to 250 kgs. Vision stated as being 'amongst the top 10 forging and machining companies globally'.
- Credit rating AA/Stable from CRISIL and ICRA; incorporated July 1979, three manufacturing facilities (Kanganwal I 1995, Kanganwal II 2006, Dugri 2021), all in Ludhiana.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Track record] Deck frames a multi-decade capability build: Rs 100 Crs revenue in 2007, Rs 500 Crs in 2018, Rs 1,000 Crs in 2023 alongside the IPO/listing, first 14,000T press line in 2022 and the 10,000-tonne forging press line commissioned in 2026.
- [Leadership] Founder Paritosh Kumar (Chairman & MD, 47+ years) with Ashish Garg (MD, joined 2006) and Megha Garg (Whole-time Director); four Chief Operating Officers listed, two of whom joined recently (2025 and 2026).
- [Certifications] Holds IATF 16949:2016, ISO 9001:2015, ISO 45001:2018, ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 9100:2018 (Aerospace Quality Management System) accreditations, plus supplier-quality awards from Dana, Ashok Leyland, Mahindra, American Axle, Escorts Kubota, TAFE, JCB and Generac.
- [Sponsor history] Secured funding through the financial sponsor route from the India Business Excellence Fund III in 2018.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin 28.6% sustained via 88% machining share, value-addition, and pricing power; raw material price drop of 3% offset by realization stability at Rs.245/kg; fixed cost leverage expected with capacity utilization rise from 59% to 75%+
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: 15-18% medium-term from new businesses; margin: sustain 28%+ EBITDA; order inflow: Rs.250cr+ new wins expected to convert in H2FY26; capex/commissioning: Rs.300cr FY26 (ex-solar), Rs.650cr total capex plan, 10k-ton & 4k-ton presses commissioning by Q2/Q3FY27
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Rs.250cr (Europe farm OEM), Rs.300cr (wind shafts), Rs.180cr/yr (industrial gensets for data centers), Rs.60cr/yr (wind components), additional PV and defense tenders in pipeline
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Wind energy (1.2-ton components), industrial gensets (data centers), defense (tender participation), EV front axle beams (35k units FY26), PV suspension components (North America)
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Despite industry headwinds in CV and farm exports, Happy Forgings delivered resilient 3.6% revenue growth and sustained 28.6% EBITDA margin through strong value-addition (88% machining share) and new wins in wind, industrial gensets, and PV segments; the Rs.650cr capacity expansion and Rs.250cr+ new order pipeline position it to capture structural demand in India's energy and EV transition.

open.item: Machining capacity reached 57,000 MT at end of H1 FY25 (from 50,000) and is expected to touch close to 62,000 MT by end of H2 FY25.
Board recommended a final dividend of Rs 4 per share (FV Rs 2) for FY26, subject to shareholder approval at the AGM.
Expects to outpace CV growth in Q3/Q4 with high single-digit growth on the domestic CV side, and high single-digit growth on the domestic farm side in FY26.
FY26 capex plan close to INR300 crores excluding solar (INR120 cr done in Q1); additional ~INR60-70 crores if solar capex fully happens this year.

North American industrial genset/power precision-machine order (~INR145 cr, ~INR30 cr annual) line is ready with testing almost over; ramp starts this quarter, ~50% utilization by Q3 and full by Q4 FY26.
Expects to deliver ~35,000 units of front axle beams this year (vs ~3,000-4,000 units in FY25), contributing ~INR30-40 crores revenue this year, rising to INR50-60 crores next year.
Won ~INR300 crores wind business (~INR60-70 crores per annum) for heavy wind shafts (150-300 kg); the wind line is being installed and starts by January of this financial year.
Expects to commission a 10,000-ton press and a 4,000-ton press this year, adding ~20,000 MTPA and taking total forging capacity to ~1,50,000 tons.
Solar captive power plant capex ongoing; 40 acres acquired and agreement signed; project expected to commence by Q1 of next financial year (targeting closure by March).
Remains on track with INR650 crores heavy-component forging facility; capex to be finished by Q2/Q3 of next financial year (FY27).
New big Hammer investment for the industrial units will come next year (FY27), probably by Q3.

Executing a Rs 650 Cr. capex programme (FY25-FY27) to build advanced forging and machining capability for heavyweight components (250 kg to 3,000 kg), targeting the heavy-forging facility commissioning by FY27.
Expects passenger vehicle segment (6% of Q1 FY26 revenue) to grow to 8%-10% of total revenues over the next two years, supported by INR80 crores capex.
Targets realization of INR275-280 per kg over the next 4-5 years on a stable steel-price basis (from INR248/kg in FY25).
Strengthening forging infrastructure through commissioning of a 10,000-tonne press (completed FY26) and a 4,000-tonne press to enhance capacity and production flexibility.
Allocated ~Rs 80 Cr. of capital expenditure to scale the passenger vehicle segment through dedicated production lines for key SUV platforms.
The new heavy-forging facility (250 kg-3,000 kg components) is expected to generate Rs 600-800 Cr. in annual revenue at optimal utilisation.
Signed a long-term lease for approximately 80-acre land to set up a captive solar plant as part of an energy transition initiative.
Announced Rs 650 Cr. investment to enter heavy forgings (>300 kg), including one of the world's largest capacity hammers.
Started participating in defense tenders for tank-application parts after receiving initial approvals; hopeful of a breakthrough soon, with larger portion once the new heavy facility starts.

verdicts.item: Management remains confident of achieving 15%-20% revenue growth over the medium term, backed by higher utilization, ongoing capex and new customer additions.
verdicts.note: Reaffirmed medium-term ('we remain bullish on a medium-term basis on kind of 15%-18%'); Q1FY26 revenue growth only 3.6%. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Expects utilization of the 14,000-ton press to rise from ~50-55% currently toward ~70% next financial year via wind business and front-axle-beam ramp-up.
verdicts.note: 14,000-ton press utilization ~46-48% (tonnage), regressed; front axle beam ramping (~35,000 units this year) but 70% FY26 target unlikely, delayed by slowdown.

verdicts.item: Expects passenger car segment (~4% of H1 revenue) to reach 8%-10% of revenues going forward in FY26-27.
verdicts.note: 'passenger vehicles segment, which contributed 6%... expect this segment to grow 8-10%... over the next two years' — on track. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Expects the wind sector business (started ~2 years ago) to become 8%-10% of company revenues over the next 2 years.
verdicts.note: 'strong demand for wind energy'; 'On the wind side... we have already won a business close to Rs.300 crores... around Rs.60 to 70 crores per annum' — wind progressing toward 8-10%.

verdicts.item: Expects total exports (20% direct + 9% deemed) to reach 30%-35% of revenues in the next 2-3 years as 60-70% of order wins are from global players.
verdicts.note: Direct exports 16% this quarter (declined with market), but new direct-export order wins (European farm, wind) support the 30-35% multi-year target. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Expects industrial segment (~12-13% of revenue) to reach 18%-20% over the next 2-3 years, led by wind gearboxes and gensets.
verdicts.note: 'Industrials, which made 13% of our revenues in this quarter... reported good growth' led by wind/power gen/oil & gas; large order wins support 18-20% over 2-3 years. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Maintains 15%-18% type revenue growth guidance sustainable on a medium term, supported by new projects and businesses.
verdicts.note: 'we remain bullish on a medium-term basis on kind of 15%-18% kind of a growth, which we have been doing in the last 10-12 years' — reaffirmed; Q1 actual 3.6%. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Expects to maintain EBITDA margins in a range of ~27%-29%; not guiding above 29% but sees gross-contribution/machining mix supporting margins.
verdicts.note: 'EBITDA margins stood at 28.6%... We remain confident of sustaining these margins going forward' — within 27-29% range.

verdicts.item: Guides to capex of INR200-250 crores per annum for FY25 and FY26.
verdicts.note: 'this year's plan is close to Rs.300 crores excluding... solar. In Q1, we have done close to Rs.120 crores' — funded internally; above INR200-250cr.

verdicts.item: The 10,000-ton press line is almost ready in Europe and will be commissioned in the next financial year (FY26).
verdicts.note: 'we expect additional commissioning for 10,000-ton press... during the year' — commissioning expected FY26.

verdicts.item: The 4,000-ton press line is a dedicated investment fully committed by one American PV customer, coming next year.
verdicts.note: 'additional commissioning for... 4,000-ton press... during the year'; ~INR110cr invested in Q1 on the new line for the PV order.

verdicts.item: Entering ring rolling/forging business (to cater to bearing industry) and plans to expand product weight range from 250 kg up to 1 tonne.
verdicts.note: Weight-range expansion progressing: 'we have already received orders from the wind sector. And these are very large components up to the weight range of 1.2 tons' (via the INR650cr facility); ring rol…
